title: Weeks 2-4 Fat-Loss and Muscle-Retention Block

goals: Continue fat loss while nutrition is managed separately.
Preserve or regain muscle and strength during the calorie deficit.
Train at the gym every weekday.
Keep each gym visit approximately 60 minutes or less.
Train core at the beginning of every gym session.
Avoid unnecessarily high-impact or high-fatigue conditioning.
confirmedHistory: Body weight reported as 106 kg before this block.
Four consecutive gym sessions were completed in the preceding Week 1.
All prescribed repetitions were reported completed with clean form.
Most Week 1 sets were conservative with more than 2-3 repetitions in reserve.
Following-day soreness was ordinary and not severe.
No accumulating leg or back fatigue was reported.
Left shoulder symptoms have no confirmed diagnosis.
Chest pressing and 35 kg neutral-grip lat pulldown produced at most slight front-left-shoulder tightness or awareness rather than pain.
The shoulder sensation disappeared essentially immediately.
No later-day or next-morning shoulder symptoms were reported.
Normal daily shoulder movement remained fine.
Frequent core work was a valued feature of previously successful programmes.
assumptions: Standard cable, selectorised resistance and cardio equipment are available.
Exact Alton Leisure Centre machine inventory has not been verified.
Machine-displayed weights are not assumed comparable between different machine models.
Nutrition is managed separately and is not modified by this prescription.
unknowns: Exact diagnosis or tissue source of historical left-shoulder symptoms.
Exact machine inventory and machine models.
Starting loads for newly introduced exercises.
Longer-term shoulder response to repeated pressing, vertical pulling and lateral-raise exposure.
constraints: No loaded overhead pressing during this block.
Do not diagnose the shoulder from exercise response.

generalRules.effortTarget: Plan Week 1: mostly 2-3 RIR. Plan Week 2: about 2 RIR. Plan Week 3: 1-2 RIR on established symptom-free exercises. Shoulder-sensitive exercises remain at 2 or more RIR.
generalRules.loadSelection: SuggestedKg values are starting anchors from previous logs, not compulsory loads. For null suggestedKg choose a conservative load that reaches the prescribed repetition range at the prescribed RIR. Never interpret null as 0 kg.
progression: Use double progression: increase repetitions within the prescribed range before increasing weight.
When every working set reaches the top of its repetition range with the prescribed RIR and clean technique on two exposures, increase by the smallest available load increment.
After increasing weight, repetitions may return toward the bottom of the range.
Do not automatically increase weight every week.
Do not progress a shoulder-sensitive movement unless its during-session and next-day response remain acceptable.
regression: If prescribed RIR cannot be maintained with clean technique, reduce the load.
If recovery deteriorates materially, hold progression before removing volume.
If necessary after holding progression, remove one working set from the affected muscle group.
If an exercise remains uncomfortable despite load and range adjustment, use its listed alternative.
symptomStopRules: Stop the provoking movement for sharp pain, increasing discomfort, unexpected weakness, instability, painful catching, numbness or tingling.
The historical 3/10 pain ceiling is not a target or proof of safety.
Brief non-painful shoulder awareness or tightness that does not increase may be logged and managed by reducing load or range.
Do not progress a movement while its shoulder response is worsening.
nextDayResponseRules: Shoulder symptoms should be no worse the following morning.
If an exercise causes a clear later-day or next-morning flare, regress or omit it at the next exposure.
Seek physiotherapy or MSK assessment if shoulder pain returns, persists, progressively worsens or causes weakness or loss of function.
missedSessionRules: Do not double sessions to catch up.
Resume with the next session in sequence.
Preserve Upper A, Lower A, lower-fatigue Wednesday, Upper B, Lower B ordering where practical.
A missed Wednesday session does not need to be made up at the weekend.
generalRules.timeRule: If the session approaches 60 minutes, shorten post-lifting cardio before removing required resistance work.
generalRules.coreRule: Core work at the beginning is a primer and direct training stimulus, not a failure circuit. Preserve approximately 3-4 RIR so it does not compromise the main lifts.

changesFromPreviousPlan.change: Five weekday gym visits are prescribed, with Wednesday deliberately lower-fatigue.
changesFromPreviousPlan.reason: Matches preferred attendance while maintaining recovery between main upper and lower sessions.

changesFromPreviousPlan.change: Core is required at the beginning of all five sessions.
changesFromPreviousPlan.reason: Frequent core training was valued and well tolerated in previous successful programmes.

changesFromPreviousPlan.change: Chest, biceps, triceps, lateral deltoids, rear deltoids and calves receive substantially more direct work.
changesFromPreviousPlan.reason: These areas were under-covered by adapted-8-week-v2.

changesFromPreviousPlan.change: The programme now uses two upper and two lower primary sessions.
changesFromPreviousPlan.reason: Improves muscle-group frequency, recovery and time efficiency.

changesFromPreviousPlan.change: Burpees, jumping lunges, mountain climbers and mandatory HIIT are absent.
changesFromPreviousPlan.reason: They are not required for the current fat-loss or muscle-retention goals and carry unnecessary fatigue or impact cost.

changesFromPreviousPlan.change: No loaded overhead press is prescribed during this block.
changesFromPreviousPlan.reason: The shoulder remains undiagnosed and only one week of current loaded upper-body tolerance is available.

changesFromPreviousPlan.change: Chest press and neutral-grip pulldown remain with monitored progression.
changesFromPreviousPlan.reason: Week 1 produced only transient non-painful awareness or tightness with no delayed symptoms.

changesFromPreviousPlan.change: Progression uses repetitions, RIR, technique and symptom response instead of automatic weekly load increases.
changesFromPreviousPlan.reason: Allows progressive overload without unnecessary fatigue or shoulder risk.

questionsBeforeStarting: Confirm in person whether the gym has a chest-supported row, cable or machine lateral-raise setup, reverse pec-deck and belt-squat machine. Use the listed alternatives when equipment is unavailable.
